context.essence: it is the exact sub-fact that keeps the root discriminant small: the new field stays within a factor of two

assertions.object: adjoining i to a number field changes the relative discriminant by a factor that divides four, only the prime two can ramify since x squared plus one gets a double root only in even residue characteristic, and so the root discriminant of the new field is at most twice the old one

context.essence: it keeps the base discriminant small: the log of the relative discriminant stays O of l log l

assertions.object: the product of the first l primes that are one mod three grows like e to the O of l log l

context.essence: it is the exact sub-fact that gives the base discriminant: conductor multiplicity for coprime conductors

assertions.object: an order three character cuts out the unique cyclic cubic subfield fixed by its kernel, and for characters whose conductors are pairwise coprime the conductors multiply, which is why the discriminant of the base field is the square of the product of the ramified primes

context.essence: it is the existence engine — the primes that split the way the tower needs, with the bad ones excluded

assertions.object: chebotarev's density theorem says the primes whose frobenius class is a prescribed element exist in infinitely many, and the finitely many ramified primes may be excluded

context.essence: it is the pigeonhole door — a bounded class group makes the many norm-one elements pile up into few classes

assertions.object: the class group of a number field has order at most the max of two and the root discriminant raised to an absolute constant times the degree, so fields of bounded root discriminant and bounded degree have class groups of bounded size

context.essence: even for a rounder ball the crossing number ceiling holds, and it is exactly tight there

assertions.object: for a strictly convex norm the crossing number bound still bounds unit pairs at a constant times n to the four thirds power, and valtr's construction attains that exponent

context.essence: it is the base of the tower — l independent cubic pieces whose galois group has l generators

assertions.object: for each prime r that is one mod three there is a unique totally real cyclic cubic subfield of the r-th cyclotomic field with conductor r, and for ramified primes that are pairwise coprime the cubic fields are linearly disjoint, the galois group of their compositum is l products of z over three, and its part over the base is the same with one generator removed

context.essence: it is the bookkeeping that keeps the tower's arithmetic small at every level

assertions.object: the absolute discriminant of a tower multiplies up the levels by the norm of the relative discriminant, the root discriminant is the discriminant raised to the reciprocal of the degree, and a step that ramifies nowhere does not change the root discriminant

context.essence: a true fact about a different norm — the ceiling changes with the shape of the unit ball

assertions.object: in a normed plane whose unit ball has a flat side point sets can have quadratically many unit pairs

context.essence: for a generic ball the count collapses to log squared growth — the far side of the norm family

assertions.object: for most norms on the plane the unit pair count grows no faster than a constant times n times log n times log log n, and in d dimensions a comeagre set of norms stays below d squared times n times log squared n with a matching lower bound up to lower order

context.essence: it tells the grid exactly which neighbor pairs are unit — the count two times m times m minus one falls out of it

assertions.object: among the points of an integer grid the unit pairs are exactly the horizontal and vertical neighbor pairs, for a diagonal step is never exactly one apart

context.essence: the first ceiling on unit pairs — a power above one but below n squared

assertions.object: because two unit circles meet in at most two points the unit pair graph of a planar set is k23 free, and the kovari sos turan theorem bounds its unit pairs at a constant times n to the three halves power

context.essence: it is the arithmetic door — many primes of the right shape split at both steps of the tower
context.source_lines: eq. (2) region (L280–295); square tables = the house bed

assertions.object: x squared plus one equals zero modulo an odd prime q has a solution exactly when q is one modulo four, and it feeds the tower: when q is one mod four and splits in the lower field then q splits in the field with i adjoined, since x squared plus one splits over the residue field

context.essence: it is the ground under the whole tower — embeddings, the totally real condition, and the integer norm fact the packing step cites

assertions.object: a number field is a finite extension of the rationals, its embeddings into the complex numbers are all different, a field is totally real when every embedding lands in the reals, and the norm of a nonzero algebraic integer is a nonzero integer of absolute value at least one

context.essence: it names the bad primes — the finite set every source statement must exclude

assertions.object: a rational prime in a field extension either splits into several distinct primes, stays inert, or ramifies, and the ramified primes are exactly the ones that divide the discriminant, a finite list

context.essence: the sharper ceiling — the crossing number pushes the exponent from three half to four third

assertions.object: the spencer szemerdi trotter crossing number count pushes the unit pair bound down to a constant times n to the four thirds power

context.essence: it is the seed of the leap — many equal-length lattice vectors come from many two-square writes

assertions.object: the products of numbers that are sums of two squares are sums of two squares in many ways

context.essence: it caps how many unit circles can share a point — the reason the unit pair graph is k23 free

assertions.object: two unit circles with different centers meet in two points when the squared distance between the centers is below four, in exactly one point when it is four, and in no point when it is above four

context.essence: it names the quantity this whole course counts

assertions.object: the number of unit pairs of a point set is the count of the pairs of its points that are exactly one apart
